problem: Express $z=5+12\text{i}$ in the form $r(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).$ Give $\theta $ in radians to three decimal places.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ We get

$$
z=\frac{1-\text{i}}{4}=\frac{1}{4}+(-\frac{1}{4})\text{i}.
$$

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=\frac{1}{4}+(-\frac{1}{4})\text{i},$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{4})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

     

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=\frac{1}{4}$ is positive and $y=-\frac{1}{4}$ is negative, $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{(-\frac{1}{4})}{(\frac{1}{4})}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the complex number $z=\frac{1-\text{i}}{4}$ in polar form:

$$
z=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{4})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{4}))
$$
